text:
The scoreboard said seven, but the chances said closer to four. Pittsburgh generated 4.29 expected goals to Philadelphia's 1.55 and still ran up a 7-0 count, which tells you the Flyers were beaten on the ice and also by a few shots that went in on lower odds. Nick Robertson's opener at 7:26 of the first was a tip-in the model gave only a 5 percent chance, and it set the tone. Replay every shot a thousand times and Pittsburgh wins about 89 percent of them, Philadelphia 11.

The game broke open in the second. Pittsburgh piled up 1.85 expected goals in the period and cashed three: Evgeni Malkin on a power-play slap shot at 5:03, Hendrix Lapierre at 7:26, and Filip Hallander at 10:23. Ville Koivunen had already made it 2-0 late in the first on a backhand. That left Dan Vladar facing 38 shots with 4.29 expected goals behind them, and he finished 2.71 goals worse than expected. Arturs Silovs, by contrast, stopped all 19 shots he saw, 1.55 goals better than an average goalie would have.

Robertson added a short-handed snap shot in the third and Egor Chinakhov finished a power-play tip-in at 16:37. Philadelphia did push back late, creating 0.76 expected goals in the third, its best period, but found nothing. Hallander, who finished with a goal and two assists and the first star, drove the night: Pittsburgh generated 1.38 expected goals while he was on the ice against just 0.39 allowed. Girard and Korczak each had two assists on the back end.
